newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says U.S. "on the verge" of budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says U.S. "on the verge" of budget deal.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said Monday the White House and Congressional Republicans were on the verge of what he said would be an historic agreement to balance the federal budget.

Four major issues remained to be resolved, Clinton told a meeting of the National Governors Association. He said any agreement must have a child-tax credit for working families, a children's health-care programme and a cigarette tax to help pay for that programme. Any agreement should keep the budget in balance in future years, he said.
"This is an historic opportunity. It can be the achievement of a generation," Clinton said. "I believe we're on the verge of achieving it."

White House and Congressional negotiators had met through the weekend to narrow their differences over the budget, and Clinton on Monday outlined provisions he said were essential for inclusion in a final deal.

"It's clear to me that it must have a child tax credit available for working families that need it," he said. "It should include $24 billion for children's health care. It should...include a tobacco tax to help pay for that health care, and it should preserve the fiscal integrity of the budget," he said.

In Washington, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Monday he hoped Congress would reach agreement with the White House and vote on any budget deal before Congress's summer recess, which is scheduled to begin next week.
